description.value: An fMRI study examined the neural activity associated with regulating negative emotional responses to stigmatized and non-stigmatized negative images, comparing stigma regulation with general emotion regulation across event-related and sustained periods.

spans.text: The current study uses functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to examine whether regulating negative bias to stigmatized individuals has a unique neural activity profile from general emotion regulation.

value: Imaging data identified widespread neural activations that were greater during the first 2 s of the decrease to stigma condition as compared with the decrease to IAPS condition.

These results demonstrated that participants had an increased neural response throughout the PFC when initially evaluating an image of a stigmatized individual than when initially evaluating an image of a non-stigmatized, negative image.
